title: Round 9 Post-Sprint Race Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Hello and welcome to today's FIA Formula 3 Press Conference following the Sprint Race in Madrid. Joining us today in third place, Alex Powell for PREMA Racing. In second place, also for PREMA Racing, James Wharton. And in first place, winner of the Sprint Race, Théophile Naël for Campos Racing. First of all, starting with you Théophile, congratulations. That was your third win of the 2026 season and you looked to be in full control after taking P1. How happy are you with that race and your performance today?

Théophile Naël: Yeah, extremely happy to be the first winner in Madrid. Obviously, it has been a really good race for me and a really good start. Then it was about managing the tyres. There is no degradation on the tyres, but just some overheating on the front-left. I still managed to set my fastest lap in the final two laps, so I am extremely happy. It means that I managed the tyres quite well and I think it is a good indication for tonight's race.

FIA Formula 3: You mentioned the fact that you were flying and you set the fastest lap of the race several times. You looked to be enjoying your time out there in Madrid, and you are now the first-ever Formula 3 race winner at this track. How does that feel, and what are your general feelings about this layout?

Naël: I was a bit disappointed about my qualifying yesterday, but obviously to bounce back like that today is such an incredible feeling. It is a home race for the team as well. We are close to becoming Teams' Champions, so these are some good points for them and also for me, maybe to fight for third place this weekend. I am very happy. The pace was really good, so I am looking forward to both races tonight and tomorrow morning.

FIA Formula 3: Like you said, unfortunately the points gap means there are now only very slim hopes for the Formula 3 title, but a top-three finish is still possible. This is the end of your second season in Formula 3. You came into it to win it, but how does a top-three finish sound?

Naël: It is not where I wanted to be, to be honest, but I think still being in the top three could be something very positive for the future as well. The pace has been there throughout the whole season. There have been some disappointing race weekends from my side, but overall I am extremely happy. Three pole positions in a row at the beginning of the season was spot on. Then we had some issues in some races and some penalties that I could have avoided. But I would still be extremely happy if I can be in the top three at the end of the weekend.

FIA Formula 3: Your team, Campos Racing, could be crowned Teams' Champions this evening after the Feature Race. That must bring a lot of satisfaction as well.

Naël: Yeah, let's see. It can be done tonight, so hopefully we do our best. I will do the best I can to grab some points, whether it is one or two. It could be done tonight, so I would be extremely happy for them.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on a great race today and best of luck for the Feature Races coming up. James, moving on to you, congratulations as well. Your second podium of 2026. You will have been hoping for one place better today in the Sprint Race, but talk us through your race this morning.

James Wharton: To be honest, it is a bit bittersweet because we were starting from pole in the first race here in Madrid, and to get that win would have been quite special. But at the same time, if you had asked me at the start of the weekend whether I would take a podium in the Sprint Race, I would have taken it. I need to be happy with the work we are doing. At the end of the day, it has not been the season that we hoped for as a team or that I hoped for as a driver. It is hard seeing people you have competed against your whole life doing well and fighting for championships, so getting these podiums when they come is very important. Apart from the start, which was not amazing, although it was not super bad, it put me on the back foot. But when you finish second on a track like this with no mistakes after the start, I have to be happy with that. You have to take those positives during a tough season.

FIA Formula 3: Turn 5 might be the best overtaking spot around the circuit. You did not quite make it stick there, but how tough is that part of the track for completing a pass?

Wharton: To be honest, it probably would have been the first overtake in Madrid ever if I had done that. It did not quite pay off, and it is obviously not easy when you are the first person to arrive there on the first lap. At the same time, I feel the races will get more and more chaotic as the season comes to an end and people are really trying to do the best they can. Starting from P12 in the Feature Race this afternoon is the next chance to get some points, so I will be the one trying to make some moves.

FIA Formula 3: Formula 3 is the first championship to race in Madrid. Was that something you had in mind starting from pole position? We did not really know what to expect because this was the first race, so was that going through your mind?

Wharton: To be honest, I really wanted to get that first win around this track. It would have been something I could take away from 2026. I did not quite get the job done, but we felt tyre degradation was going to be a big issue. We thought there would be some, but it was not as clear as we expected, so maybe I could have pushed a little more at the start of the race. The lack of knowledge was quite tough. Normally, we go into a race really understanding what happened in previous years, but today we did not have that, so we were learning during the race itself. As you saw with Théophile, he kept getting faster. At the same time, we have to take the podium today. That is all we could have done.

FIA Formula 3: Will the Feature Race be easier with the data you collected, or perhaps more difficult because of the physical challenge of having to race again?

Wharton: It is obviously going to be a very different race. Starting P12 and starting P1 make for very different races. If you ask any driver, starting in that part of the grid is always more difficult. You have to be a little more careful with the people around you. But I feel there are opportunities to be had in this Feature Race at 6 p.m., when everyone has been awake since 6 a.m. Hopefully, everyone is a little more tired and some more mistakes happen, which is what we can capitalise on today.

FIA Formula 3: We will leave it there for now. Congratulations. Alex, thank you for waiting. Your first FIA Formula 3 podium, with P3 in the Sprint Race, in only your second round in the Championship. How satisfied are you with that result today?

Alex Powell: Of course, it is super cool to be on the podium. It was unexpected. Obviously, it was very last-minute to join for the final two rounds, but we have been pretty competitive since the start of the weekend, from Free Practice. We had pretty good potential and yesterday qualifying was executed pretty well. Today it was just about staying out of trouble and learning about tyre management, which is quite new for me as well. Then it was about staying clean and making it to the end of the race.

FIA Formula 3: Monza, the last race weekend, was your first round in Formula 3. We come here to Madrid, where the Formula 3 test took place a few weeks ago. Did this weekend feel a little easier because you knew the track and how the car would behave?

Powell: For sure. I think it is helpful for me, seeing as it is new for everyone. Monza was definitely a baptism of fire. It was a weekend of firsts, so it was about learning as much as possible. This weekend, I knew there was probably going to be a bit more opportunity. I am glad we capitalised on it in the Sprint Race, but of course we have two more races to look forward to and we will try to extract a little more.

FIA Formula 3: Looking at how the Sprint Race went this morning, what are your hopes for the Feature Race, and how do you think it will unfold for you starting from P11?

Powell: I think it is going to be an interesting one. Of course, we have the information from the Sprint Race, which can help us, but at the end of the day overtaking is quite tricky around here. It is just going to be about capitalising on other people's mistakes and looking forward, trying to make every opportunity count. We will see where we end up.

FIA Formula 3: Let's see. Thank you very much.

title: Taito Kato: 'We can win the Feature Races' after impressing in Madrid so far
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix's Taito Kato is thriving around the challenging Madring circuit, as the Japanese driver came from P12 on the Sprint Race grid to secure points.

Kato pulled off a brave overtake at Turn 5, rounding MP Motorsport's Tuukka Taponen for P10, before gaining another position once Enzo Delingy’s 10-second time penalty took effect.

Reflecting on his race, the Honda Formula Dream Project driver said he was happy with the overtake and added points to his 2026 tally.

"I think it was really great. Overall, really difficult to overtake here and I think you saw that in the race. There was no overtaking point, and really difficult to overtake the car in front, even with DRS.

"We had a good start and gained some points. I was able to overtake Pedro and then at that point, I was P11. Then, Lap 12 or 13 I was able to overtake Tuukka in front because he didn't have DRS.

"I had good top speed, I could go side-by-side into T5 and then brake later to move in front. But it was really tough to be honest. But happy to finally have gained the position."

Kato was one of the few overtakes in what was a tricky Sprint around the Madring. The ART driver said that the race was hugely important in terms of building data ahead of the first Feature Race on Saturday evening, and Sunday morning.

He added that he will need to work very hard with the team both during and after the race in order to extract the maximum performance in Sunday's event, as he targets a final round leap up to third in the Drivers' Championship.

"It's going to be the same situation in the two Feature Races I guess. I will just focus on the tyre saving and also managing the gap in front and behind.

"Good communication with the engineers. When you have to close or not because we need to get some data for the other Feature Race.

"So we need to get clean air. Because we start in P1 in the Feature Race, and P4 in the other Feature too. I think it's quite a different story as it was a Sprint Race. So we can gather as much data as we can.

"We had really good data from the Sprint Race. So I think we have really good car performance and good confidence for the two races.

"For sure we can get another win. We have a really good mindset from the Monza. Obviously, it was a mighty weekend in Monza. But still, I couldn't win the Feature Race. So I think this time the target is to win in the Feature."

title: SPRINT RACE: Nael in full control for third win of 2026
excerpt:
Théophile Nael earned the first ever race win around the Madring, taking the lead on the opening lap and controlling things from the front.

It was the Campos Racing driver's third win of the season, as PREMA Racing's James Wharton and Alex Powell completed the podium on a strong day for the Italian team.

AS IT HAPPENED

Wharton got a decent start from pole position, but it was Nael with the best launch, and he claimed the lead into Turn 1.

The Australian went wheel-to-wheel with the Frenchman into Turn 5 but went deep and had to skip across the chicane. The PREMA driver ceded the position later in the lap and was able to slot back into second ahead of teammate Powell.

The title contenders didn't make progress on the opening lap, with Ugo Ugochukwu retaining P9 while Freddie Slater dropped one position to 18th in the TRIDENT.

By Lap 5, Nael had extended his lead over the chasing PREMAs to over a second, putting him out of DRS range to the tune of 1.3s.

Alessandro Giusti had been running fourth but was told over team radio to cede the position to Bruno Del Pino. The Frenchman obliged out of Turn 17, dropping back to fifth and keeping Ernesto Rivera in his mirrors.

Having dropped out of DRS range to Del Pino, Giusti was coming under pressure from Rivera and the Mexican was told to attack by the Campos team over the radio on Lap 9.

Nael took the lead of the race into Turn 1 and never looked in trouble after the opening laps

Overtaking was proving tough, but Taito Kato showed it was possible, rounding Tuukka Taponen with DRS into Turn 5 to take the final points place in 10th.

Seventh on the road Enzo Deligny was then handed a 10-second time penalty on Lap 13 for leaving the track and gaining an advantage in an earlier defence of P7 from Jin Nakamura.

At the front though, nobody could catch Nael, who took fastest lap as well as race victory in a dominant display around the Madring.

PREMA Racing's Wharton and Powell rounded out the podium, the latter earning his maiden rostrum visit on his second weekend in F3.

Del Pino held off Giusti and Rivera for fourth. Deligny's penalty dropped him to 15th, promoting Nakamura, Ugochukwu, Kato and Taponen up once position each in the points.

Nael's win was his third of the 2026 campaign and lifted him to third in the Standings

KEY QUOTE - Théophile Nael, Campos Racing

"First victory of the weekend is for me. Super happy to take the first win around the Madring and another podium. The car was mega! I managed to have a really good start and then managed the tyres towards the end and also had the best lap of the race as well, so very happy."

THE CHAMPIONSHIP STANDINGS

Freddie Slater remains at the top of the Drivers' Championship on 141 points, but Ugo Ugochukwu takes a potentially vital two points out of his lead in P2, going onto 129. Théophile Nael's victory lifts him up to third ahead of Campos teammate Ernesto Rivera, 86 points to 81. Taito Kato remains fifth in the Standings on 73.

Campos Racing closes in on their second-consecutive Teams' title, extending their lead and going onto 296 points. TRIDENT is second on 213, with Van Amersfoort Racing taking third with 162. ART Grand Prix is now fourth on 157 points, with MP Motorsport fifth on 138.

UP NEXT

The FIA Formula 3 drivers are back in action later on Saturday with the first of two Feature Races this weekend. Taito Kato goes from Pole Position, while Ugo Ugochukwu will be aiming to take over the lead of the Drivers' Championship from P4 on the grid.

title: Deligny revels in ‘best qualifying of the year’ after strong performance in Madrid
excerpt:
Enzo Deligny qualified in the top six for both Madrid Feature Races after a strong qualifying performance

Enzo Deligny was delighted with the “best” and most “fun” qualifying of the season, with the Van Amersfoort Racing driver in strong position for all three races.

The French driver was fifth in Qualifying 1 and sixth in Qualifying 2, and after a tough run of results on Friday, he is delighted to finally show his potential.

“It’s the best quali of the year for me,” he said. “It was definitely my point to work on this year, so this is nice for the confidence, as it's for sure not an easy track.

“To be able to have two very solid qualifyings at the end of the year I think it's good for the morale and the confidence as well.

“It was the most fun quali of the year as well. I like the back-to-back qualis, obviously if it goes well in the first one.

Deligny was strong throughout both Qualifying sessions much to his delight

“But it's nice because you start with quite a heavy car, almost a full tank. You feel the fuel going down every lap and you're just fine-tuning every lap. So, honestly, it was really fun. The sunset as well made it quite cinematic, so it was cool.”

When asked what had changed to improve his qualifying form this weekend, Deligny believed that it was being in a positive place with the car that helped him feel more comfortable.

READ MORE

Alex Powell eyeing up Sprint Race possibilities after impressive Madrid Qualifying

Round 11 Post Qualifying 2 Press Conference

“I just felt really comfortable and confident in the car,” he said. “I was able to drive how I wanted to whereas a lot of qualis before the summer, I was quite confused in the car and wasn't sure why it was reacting in a certain way.

“But we've put in a lot of work with the team, so I'm really happy to at least finish the year with a strong quali.”

The VAR driver has his eyes on scoring big points across the three races

Looking ahead to the three races, Deligny is excited with his strong starting positions, believing it gives him a chance to end the season on a high.

“I think it will be mainly about the start tomorrow,” he continued. “So let's see. Our starts are usually not bad. But otherwise, I think the races are going to be quite like Monaco, not much overtaking.

“But let's see. I'm not fighting for anything too meaningful in the championship. So I'll just have fun, try and move forward if I can. But otherwise, I think most of the job was done today and just bring it home in the races.”

Next Up

title: Round 11 Post Qualifying 2 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA Formula 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following Qualifying Session 2 here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from Rodin Motorsport is Pedro Clerot. In second place, from Campos Racing, is Ugo Ugochukwu, and from MP Motorsport, capturing his second pole position of the season, is Tuukka Taponen. Congratulations, Tuukka. How does that one feel?

Tuukka Taponen: Yeah, it feels good. P3 in Q1 and P1 in the second qualifying. To be honest, I felt better with the driving in Q1, but luckily it was enough in Q2 to secure pole position. I am super happy to start on pole for Sunday's race.

FIA Formula 3: Can you take me through that pole-winning lap? How much commitment did it take from you?

Taponen: Yeah, I was one tenth off before starting the last push, and I was fifth or sixth. It was very tight there. We have been struggling the whole week in sector one, so it was just trying to minimise the time lost there and then do a good rest of the lap, which I did. It was a good lap at the end.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on that pole position. Ugo, coming to you next, congratulations. You have set yourself up well for a run at this championship. How good was the car for you today?

Ugo Ugochukwu: Yeah, for sure, it was a positive day for us. Two good qualifying sessions are exactly what we needed. I think we executed everything well, with no mistakes, and I got the lap in when we needed it. I am pretty happy overall and pretty happy with my lap. I think I maximised it to the limit. Some of the others were quite quick today, so P4 and P2, we will take it. I think we can look forward to the races and maximise our points.

FIA Formula 3: Moving on to the races, what is the mindset heading in? Is it the championship?

Ugochukwu: Yeah, for sure. I think two clean, or three clean races would be nice, picking up the points along the way. But we will see how the race unfolds. These are going to be the first races here in Madrid, so we do not fully know what to expect on the racing side. We will see if on Sunday we have an opportunity to go for the win. It would be nice to get another one under our belt. But overall, of course, points are the main thing. It is no secret that is what is going to get us the championship.

FIA Formula 3: And just your thoughts on the circuit. Do you have a favourite corner?

Ugochukwu: I would have to say Turns 10 and 11, before Monumental, the fast chicane. That is a super-tricky corner, and you can gain quite a bit of time when you are on the limit. We were quite quick through sector two, so maybe I am a little bit biased as well.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P2. Pedro, coming to you, congratulations on P3. Can you take me through your final push run and what happened in the last corner?

Pedro Clerot: Yeah, I felt comfortable throughout the qualifying session, and I knew I had done a really good sector one by that time. I think that was our strong point, and I was chasing that feeling the whole day. I finally managed to do it on the last push of qualifying. I knew I was P2 at that time, less than a tenth behind Ugo, so I just committed for the whole lap. I was losing a bit of grip throughout the lap. On the previous lap, I think I was already quite sideways in the last sector. I just lost the rear of the car. Fortunately, by then it was the end of the session, so we did not really get affected. I think we would have been in the fight for pole with that lap, but I am just happy to be at the front again. We showed really good speed. We showed that we were up there in both qualifying sessions. It was a bit of a sad end, but I am happy that we could deliver when it mattered.

FIA Formula 3: Did you notice any track evolution through the session?

Clerot: For sure. We went, I think, almost a second quicker than Q1. Obviously, Q1 was a little bit messier. At least, I got fewer push laps in Q1. Q2 was a bit cleaner on my side and the driving felt a little bit better. But for sure, there was some track evolution since free practice today. We saw a big change in the times, so it was a bit different for us after two F1 sessions and two F2 sessions. It was the first time for us. I think we managed to do everything well today, and the results paid off.

title: Round 9 Post-Qualifying 1 Press Conference
excerpt:
FIA FORMULA 3: Welcome everyone to today's FIA Formula 3 press conference following Qualifying Session 1 here in Madrid. Joining us in P3 from MP Motorsport is Tuukka Taponen. In second place, from Rodin Motorsport, is Pedro Clerot. And from ART Grand Prix, capturing his first pole position in Formula 3, is Taito Kato. Taito, congratulations. How does that one feel?

Taito Kato: It feels amazing. My first-ever pole position in Formula 3. It was an amazing weekend in Monza, and then back-to-back this weekend in Madrid. I think we have a good mindset, and the car was incredible during qualifying and really fun to drive here. In Madrid, you are really close to the wall. I was pushing on the edge, sometimes kissing the wall. That was really good. Finally, to get pole position, I am very happy with it.

FIA FORMULA 3: It is the first pole position for ART Grand Prix since Hungary 2024. How was the car today? You said it was good, but did it take a lot to get it into a window where you felt confident with it?

Kato: I think it was really good the whole year. There were just mistakes on my side, some traffic, or a bit of bad luck. Every time in Formula 3, it is really difficult to put everything together in one lap. Also, if you do not have any luck, it is really difficult to get pole position. So, finally, to get pole position in Formula 3, I am happy with the team and just want to say a massive thanks to the team. The car was incredible.

FIA FORMULA 3: The first-ever F3 qualifying here in Madrid. What did you make of the circuit?

Kato: Really good. Really, really fun to drive. The adrenaline was incredible in the car.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on the pole position. P2, Pedro Clerot, congratulations. Just 12-thousandths away from pole position. Can you take me through your session?

Pedro Clerot: Yeah, very close. I think it was an overall good session. It was a bit messy where I was. I only managed to do one push lap, and that was the one I had to make count. Together with the team, we saw that today was going to be all about putting a lap on the board, and I think we managed to do quite well. I felt really comfortable from free practice, and I knew the pace was there. Even though we were not so high up in free practice, I knew we were going to be okay. The car came alive in qualifying, and I was actually quite surprised to see I was P1 after the first run. I could not do my second lap because of traffic, and I could see on the TV that Kato was improving. I was thinking, please do not improve by too much. I could see it was just a small difference, but I am happy to be starting on the front row and happy for the team as well. We put a lot of work into this weekend, and it paid off.

FIA Formula 3: What did it feel like to drive the car on the limit in qualifying here?

Clerot: Very nice. Very, very nice. Overall, I am very happy for the team as well. Driving here is unique. You are close to every single wall. The more you risk, the higher the reward. Even though my lap was, I am not going to say on the safe side, but a very controlled lap, I was on the edge already. There was not a lot more in it, and for sure it feels really good to piece together a good lap around this place.

FIA Formula 3: Congratulations on P2. P3, Tuukka Taponen. Tuukka, congratulations. How was that session for you?

Tuukka Taponen: Yeah, that was quite an alright session. I missed the first lap because I made a mistake, but after that it was quite clean for me. There was not any traffic, and all the laps I did were quite okay. I feel like my driving was better in this qualifying than in Q2, but it was quite okay, let us say.

FIA Formula 3: And just your thoughts on the circuit, on the track here. What did you think?

Taponen: It is a special track. You do not have any other tracks like that. You have many difficult corners, and like Taito said, it is very difficult to put everything together at this circuit. You just need to be good everywhere.

title: Alex Powell eyeing up Sprint Race possibilities after impressive Madrid Qualifying
excerpt:
Alex Powell put in one of the stand-out performances in Madrid Qualifying, finishing P10 in the first session to secure a second row start for the Sprint Race.

In what was just his second FIA Formula 3 Qualifying session, the PREMA Racing driver was on the pace from the outset, fighting for the top places.

Reflecting on the day, Powell said that he was very pleased with his and the team's performance, and that he felt a good result was a possibility from the opening laps of the weekend.

"A couple weeks ago I didn't even know I would be here," Powell said. "So very last minute, happy with the whole session to be honest. It was really strong for the whole team.

READ MORE

QUALIFYING: Kato takes pole in Q1 with Taponen on top in Q2; Ugochukwu seizes advantage in title fight

"We struggled a little bit this morning in Practice so I was a bit skeptical going into quali but the car was working really well, and I was happy with my driving.

"I think of course in retrospect I could have done a few things better but if I would have known I would have been a top 10 a couple weeks ago, I would have definitely taken it and signed the paper. So it's a good step for me, a good step forward but of course the aim is going to be to keep building from here."

After in-season testing last month, Practice offered the drivers one final look at the Madring circuit ahead of the Qualifying sessions.

With two grid-setting sessions this weekend, any mistake would have had a major impact, and Powell was pleased to have kept himself out of trouble whilst showing impressive pace.

The PREMA driver was P10 in Qualifying 1 around Madrid after an impressive performance

"It was very difficult in Practice to build things up. I felt really good though from the first push which was very nice, especially at a street circuit, you kind of have to have the rhythm from very early on.

"So I was really, really happy that I could feel a good rhythm from the very first push and then it was just about sustaining and building on that but we were pretty strong the whole time."

Though the PREMA driver was happy with his final Qualifying positions, he is targeting better things in the Sprint Race.

With a second row start and overtaking opportunities expected to be at a premium around the Spanish venue, Powell hopes to convert his starting position into a memorable result in just his second weekend.

"Looking back on it, I could have found a little bit here and a little bit there, but I'm sure everyone could say the same thing. Of course, as the session goes on, the intensity rises and you start to take a little bit more risk.

"I just missed a few tenths here and there to finish a little bit higher up but still it was a clean session for me, with no major scary moments let's say.

"The goal will be to move forward. We're on the second row of the grid for the Sprint, but the goal is still to move forward. The tyre management is still new to me, but I think I'm in a good position to make it work, so eyes forward."

title: QUALIFYING: Kato takes pole in Q1 with Taponen on top in Q2; Ugochukwu seizes advantage in title fight
excerpt:
ART Grand Prix driver Taito Kato claimed his maiden FIA Formula 3 Aramco Pole Position Award with a stunning performance in Qualifying 1, completing a 1:50.535 to beat Pedro Clerot by 0.012s.

In Qualifying 2, MP Motorsport driver Tuukka Taponen impressively beat title hopeful Ugo Ugochukwu to the Aramco Pole Position Award for Feature Race 2.

The Campos Racing driver was also fourth in Q1, while his rival Freddie Slater struggled, finishing 17th in the opening session, and eighth in Q2.

QUALIFYING 1

Kato was the first driver to cross the line and completed a 1:51.127. But no one else could match the ART driver with Alex Powell 0.161s behind in second.

It was not good news for TRIDENT, with Noah Stromsted’s sidepod coming loose after contact on the warmup lap with Kanato Le, while Slater complained of issues with the car.

On the second set of laps, Kato improved to a 1:50.639, with Jin Nakamura 0.218s behind in P2.

The Japanese drivers were demoted a position moments later when Rodin Motorsport’s Clerot went quickest on a 1:50.547.

In the battle for the title Slater was down in P11. The Championship leader was still complaining of issues with his car.

TRIDENT brought their driver in and fitted him with a new set of Hard tyres, while the rest of the field continued on.

Kato improved to a 1:50.535 to eclipse Clerot by 0.012s as Ugochukwu went to P4. Slater, despite the new rubber, came on the radio to complain of issues on his TRIDENT.

Elsewhere, Brando Badoer’s session looked to be over after he hit the barrier, with Rodin left in a race against time to fix his left rear suspension ahead of Qualifying 2.

Out on track, Kato could not improve on his final lap of Q1. But neither could his rivals, leaving him on pole for Feature Race 1, with Clerot settling for P2 ahead of Taponen.

Ugochukwu was fourth in front of Enzo Deligny, as Jin Nakamura followed in sixth ahead of Ernesto Rivera and Alessandro Giusti. Bruno del Pino ended up in P9, heading Alex Powell and Théophile Nael, while James Wharton rounded out the top 12.

The PREMA Racing driver is set to start Saturday’s Sprint Race from reverse grid pole, with Q1 setting the grid for the first race of the weekend.

In the title fight, Slater’s struggles continued, with a lockup at Turn 1 leaving him down in P17 in the first Qualifying session, much to his frustration.

QUALIFYING 2

After a short break the drivers were back out on track. This included Slater with TRIDENT having worked to fix his car in the break between the sessions.

The British driver looked to be back in the groove as he completed a 1:49.972 to go fastest, with Ugochukwu in second, over half a second behind his title rival.

Clerot and Badoer, who was back out on track with his car fixed, went up to second and third, although Nakamura split the Rodin duo moments later.

On the second set of laps, Kato jumped up to P1 only for Ugochukwu to demote him to P2 moments later with a 1:49.901.

Clerot continued his strong form to take over at the top with a 1:49.830. Slater, having set the fastest first sector, locked up on the entry to Turn 5, leaving him fifth.

Ugochukwu then reclaimed P1 with a 1:49.771 as Slater aborted his lap and returned to the pit lane. Clerot finished his next lap to go to P2, 0.069s off the Campos driver.

On the final lap of the day, Taponen went quickest on a 1:49.750. Ugochukwu came across the line but could not improve and stayed second.

Behind them, Clerot had been on for a fast lap, but he pushed too hard at the final corner, winding up in the barriers, bringing the session to an end.

This left Taponen on pole for Feature Race 2 ahead of Ugochukwu and Clerot, with Kato in fourth ahead of Mattia Colnaghi. Deligny was sixth ahead of Giusti and Slater, with Yevan David in P9. Rivera was 10th ahead of Badoer and Powell.

The first race of the Madrid weekend is on Saturday morning with lights out for the Sprint set for 11:05 local time.

title: PRACTICE: Nakamura fastest for Hitech in Madrid ahead of Kato
excerpt:
Jin Nakamura started the Madrid weekend fastest of all for Hitech. The Japanese driver recorded a 1:49.835 in the final minutes of the session to lead compatriot Taito Kato for ART Grand Prix by a tenth. Van Amersfoort Racing's Enzo Deligny completed the top three.

Kato was the first to set a time in the session, with the ART driver leading an early 1-2-3 for the French team on a 1:53.026.

The Japanese driver lowered his time to a 1:52.026 which was then bettered by Tuukka Taponen by just 0.037s.

Kato then returned to the top with 15 minutes to run on a 1:51.567 before title contender Ugo Ugochukwu went fastest with a 1:51.192.

The Campos Racing driver was flying on his next lap as he shaved off over half a second on his next attempt to lead the pack on a 1:50.587 with teammate Ernesto Rivera in P2.

Championship leader Freddie Slater replied with 20 minutes to go, lowering the benchmark effort to a 1:50.453.

Pedro Clerot had an earlier time good enough for P3 deleted, but he restored himself to the top three with just over 15 minutes to go with Taponen and then Rodin Motorsport teammate Brando Badoer in the top five.

Kato then went quickest once again, 0.060s ahead of Slater's time, before Fionn McLaughlin went just behind Clerot for Hitech in fifth.

Ugochukwu logged a 1:50.268 on his next lap to return to the top, before title rival Slater bettered that by just 0.072s.

Into the final five minutes and Enzo Deligny went to P2 just 0.069s off top spot before the next set of improvements arrived.

Kato lowered his best to a 1:49.936 to go P1, as Ugochukwu finished 0.064s down on that time in P2, 0.002s ahead of Rivera, with Slater fourth.

Nakamura then went quickest in the final minute, with Deligny moving himself back to third just as the Red Flag was thrown.

A crash for Nicola Lacorte in the final seconds brought Practice to a close, with the DAMS Lucas Oil driver OK after tagging the barriers at the exit of Turn 9.

Nakamura led Kato, Deligny, Ugochukwu and Rivera in the top five. Slater followed in sixth ahead of McLaughlin, Taponen, Clerot and Bruno Del Pino in the top 10.

There will be two Qualifying sessions this weekend, with the first getting underway at 18:25 local time. The second will follow immediately afterwards, with the green light scheduled for 18:55 local time.

title: PREVIEW: Round 9 in Madrid brings it all to a close
excerpt:
It is the final race weekend of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 season, and the paddock is heading to Madrid for what should to be an epic title showdown.

Freddie Slater and Ugo Ugochukwu look set to go head-to-head to be crowned Drivers’ Champion, while Campos Racing are on the brink of winning the Teams’ Title, but can TRIDENT stop them?

So as we get ready to hit the track in Madrid, here is everything you need to know…

WHAT TO EXPECT

Round 9 kicks off with Free Practice on Friday morning with the green light set for 09:55 local time.

There will be a slight twist to the weekend format in Madrid, as we will have two Feature Races, which means we have two Qualifying sessions.

The first of which is set to start at 18:25 local time. After those first 20 minutes of action, the drivers will hit the track for the second Qualifying session at 18:55 local time.

The top 12 from Qualifying 1 will be reversed for Saturday morning’s Sprint Race at 11:05 local time. That session will also set the grid for the first Feature Race at 18:00 later that day.

Qualifying 2 will set the order for second and final Feature Race of the weekend, with lights out scheduled for 09:45 local time on Sunday morning.

Niccolò Maccagnani is set to replace Christian Ho at Rodin Motorsport for the final round of the season.

AIX Racing have confirmed that Car 26 has been withdrawn from the event as Ricardo Escotto cannot take part under medical grounds.

DAMS Lucas Oil have also withdrawn Car 31 from the race weekend.

STAT PACK

The Madring is made up of 22 corners and is 5.414km long.

The drivers got their first taste of the circuit at a two-day test last month where Campos Racing’s Ugo Ugochukwu set the fastest time of a 1:49.034.

Ugochukwu led both morning sessions during last month’s test, while Slater topped the timesheets in the afternoon runs.

Slater and Ugochukwu head into the finale separated by 15 points, with Ernesto Rivera and Théophile Nael still retaining an outside chance of claiming the title.

With Nicola Lacorte’s victory at Monza, 13 different drivers have now won a race in 2026 — a new record for the most winners in a single Formula 3 season.

FROM THE GRID – Bruno del Pino, Van Amersfoort Racing

“It’s very fast, really fast. But it’s also tight, it feels like Jeddah in a way. But it’s a home race so that’s exciting.

“There are not many places to overtake, because the run to T1 is not a very long, but there's a very long straight afterwards. So maybe there.

“I’d say the most difficult part will be making use of the high-speed sections and getting close to the walls, but everything else will be quite quick and easy to adapt.

“It's my home race. I have two home race weekends. So, Barcelona, because I was born there, and Madrid because I'm half from Madrid, and I live in Madrid. It is exciting.”

TECHNICAL PREVIEW

Pierre-Alain Michot, FIA Formula 3 Technical Director

“While it is a new track on the calendar the Madring is known to the drivers and the teams as they had two days of in-season testing here last month.

“It is a high-speed street track with many changes of directions, which means the teams will put a huge emphasis on downforce, making sure their cars are aerodynamically balanced in both Qualifying and the races.

“Tyres will also be a point of focus, with temperatures expected to be high, and with nature of the layout, those who take care of their Pirelli rubber will benefit the most.”

PIRELLI PREVIEW

The Hard compound has been selected for the Formula 3 weekend at Madring. Drivers have already had a first taste of the new circuit in the Spanish capital during the two-day test held at the end of August. Tyre degradation is expected to remain limited and, should temperatures be relatively low, aided by the circuit's altitude, graining could become a factor. Qualifying could prove to be one of the most decisive and demanding sessions of the weekend, given the limited overtaking opportunities offered by the circuit. Furthermore, as this is a new track on which drivers still have limited experience, the likelihood of safety car interventions and red flags remains high.

title: Escotto and Xie withdrawn from Madrid round
excerpt:
Ricardo Escotto and Gerrard Xie have both been withdrawn from Round 9 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 season.

Both AIX Racing and DAMS Lucas Oil confirmed that both drivers would not participate in Madrid this weekend.

Escotto was involved in a road traffic accident, and based on medical advice, will not be in the car this weekend.

Kenny Kirwan, AIX Racing Formula 3 Team Manager said of Escotto’s withdrawal: “First and foremost, our thoughts are with Ricardo following his recent traffic collision. On behalf of everyone at AIX Racing, I would like to wish him a smooth and speedy recovery. His health and wellbeing are, above all else, the priority at this time.

“Unfortunately, as a result of this incident, Ricardo will not be able to participate in the upcoming Madring Formula 1 support event, which is the final round of the FIA Formula 3 Championship. Our thoughts are firmly with him and his family as he focuses on his recovery, and we would like to thank Ricardo for his commitment and contribution to AIX Racing. We wish him all the very best for his recovery and for the next chapter of his career.”

Both AIX and DAMS will enter two cars each this weekend in Madrid.

title: Title would be ‘icing on the cake’ says Ugochukwu after strong season with Campos
excerpt:
Ugo Ugochukwu says his mindset going into Madrid is to win two Feature Races as he gets set to fight for the title this weekend.

The Campos Racing driver is just 15 points behind leader Freddie Slater and with 67 points available this weekend with there being two Feature Races.

For Ugochukwu, the mindset is simple: to be as quick as possible.

“Feeling good, feeling up for it,” said Ugochukwu when asked about his mindset going into the weekend. “I think this is the moment that the whole season kind of comes down to, this last round where you need to step it up in terms of performance.

“But the feeling is pretty good. I think on our side, we don't have much to lose on my side.

“I'm just going to go for it and try to be as quick as possible. So my focus is just on trying to be in the front row in quali and then go for the race win. That's going to maximise our points.”

Ugochukwu says the Madrid weekend feels like the opening round in Melbourne that he won

Ugochukwu and Campos had a good two days of testing in Madrid last month, with the American setting the fastest time across the two days.

As a pairing they bring a lot of confidence with them to the track this time around, knowing what they can do if they put it together.

“Feeling good for the weekend, for sure,” he said. “I think there's definitely some points to catch up on, but I'm still confident that it's definitely possible to get the job done.

READ MORE

‘I want to win this’ - Slater excited for the title fight at Madring

Ugo Ugochukwu: Turning a tough rookie season into a title-contending campaign

“Coming off a good test always helps. I feel pretty nailed around the track. We'll see in FP how the weekend starts and evolves with the F1 grip now. But I'm getting Melbourne vibes for some reason to this weekend, and that went pretty well.

“It was the first race of the season, everyone was excited to get it going, and this is kind of similar.

“It’s the last one, and everyone wants to end very well, and it’s just time to do it now.”

Ugochukwu spoke about his mindset going into the weekend

Ugochukwu and Slater have gone wheel-to-wheel several times over the season as they battle for the title.

When asked what the mindset will be if the two have to fight out on track for the top prize, the 19-year-old says the main thing will be to avoid unnecessary risks.

“Well, as I said, it depends a little bit on the situation,” said Ugochukwu. “I think being the one behind, you want to finish the races to kind of outscore your rival.

“So you don't really want to be taking too many on track battle risks. I'll try to be further you are in the front or P1. That's how you kind of avoid those risks. So that'll make the weekend a lot cleaner if I'm going off the front.”

Ugochukwu comes into the final round with two victories – including a record breaking 17s win in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

Ugochukwu showed good pace during the in-season test in Madrid last month

On top of that, the American has six podiums and has numerous highlights in wheel-to-wheel battles. He feels if he were to be holding the biggest trophy come the end of the year, it would be a nice touch on a strong season.

“I think through the year we definitely showed that the pace was there,” he said. “We had strong results, and also the consistency was there, to be battling for the title, you need to be consistently getting the points.

READ MORE

Freddie Slater: How the rookie’s title bid has taken shape in 2026

What To Watch For: A few key talking points ahead of the title decider in Madrid

“For sure, the championship will be a nice little icing on the cake. I think pure mindset is trying to get two Feature Race wins.

“That's what's on our mind, because if we can get that, there's a good chance that the title will come with it. So I think the title kind of comes later, and then just the pure focus on the weekend is the main thing on our mindset.”

title: ‘I want to win this’ - Slater excited for the title fight at Madring
excerpt:
Freddie Slater is “buzzing” for the title fight in Madrid, with the TRIDENT driver on the cusp of being crowned Formula 3 champion this weekend.

The British driver comes to the circuit 15 points clear of title rival Ugo Ugochukwu, with there being a possibility of him taking the title on Saturday.

As the 18-year-old previewed the racing action, he also reflected on his season to date, and why he is proud to be in the position he is in now.

“I'm buzzing,” said Slater ahead of the weekend. “I think obviously last weekend was what it was, and we could have been in a much better position going into this weekend. But that's in the past and now we focus on this weekend.

“I've done an incredible job all year. The team has done an incredible job as well. For the results we've had, we've had eight podiums in eight weekends.

“We've been on the front row in however many qualifyings. It's been an incredible rookie season. So to put ourselves in a championship, the pressures on everyone else as a rookie, it's just having fun and maximising results.

Slater is incredibly proud of the season that he and TRIDENT have had

“There's a lot of other things that other people need to prove, but for me it's just about trying to fight for this championship and win it on Sunday.”

Slater got his first taste of the Madring last month at the in-season test, and he topped two of the four sessions across the two days of running.

READ MORE

Ugo Ugochukwu: Turning a tough rookie season into a title-contending campaign

Freddie Slater: How the rookie’s title bid has taken shape in 2026

When asked about the circuit, Slater said: “I love it. I think it's one of the best tracks on the calendar. It's one of the most exciting. It's old school. It's got character.

“It's one of the most exhilarating to drive and it's nice to get a new track that actually has that to it. It gives you a real buzz when you drive it on the qualifying lap.

“So honestly, I can't wait for qualifying, a sunset qualifying, which is going to be quite late. “The track's going to be fast, cars are going to be fast, low fuel, everything. So it's going to be an enjoyable one.”

The British driver has set his sights on ending the season with the championship

Slater comes into the weekend with eight podiums from all eight rounds, and he believes a title at the end of the round would be the perfect ending to a great campaign.

“I think I've proven everything that I've needed to,” he said. “I've done an amazing job all year. I'm not a person that always gives myself a lot of credit, but honestly, when I look back on this year, the things I've done in my control have been really well executed.

“Now we want to go fight for a championship. I don't want to finish second and I want to win this thing. So I'm going to do everything in my power, everything that we can to try and win it. I'm definitely going to leave anything out there.”

title: Ugo Ugochukwu: Turning a tough rookie season into a title-contending campaign
excerpt:
A look at a few of the factors that have helped Ugo Ugochukwu fight for the title ahead of the final round in Madrid

By Sunday night Ugo Ugochukwu could be the FIA Formula 3 Champion.

For that to happen, he has to overturn a 15-point deficit to leader Freddie Slater, with the two set to go head-to-head at the final round in Madrid.

The Campos Racing driver’s year has been on excellent race pace, and early season consistency. His and the team’s form has taken a slight dip of late, but there are signs they are rediscovering their best at the right time.

So here’s how Ugochukwu has built his campaign…

BUILDING ON THE MOMENTUM OF 2025

This is Ugochukwu’s second season in Formula 3, as he returned after a tough rookie year. The American made the step up with a huge reputation as a Macau Grand Prix winner and Euro 4 champion, so to go the first half of 2025 with just two points finishes would have been tough.

The American got his season off to a fine start with a victory in the Melbourne Feature Race

However the second part of the campaign was much better. He achieved several more points finishes, including two Sprint podiums, and a couple of front row starts at Silverstone and Monza.

Rediscovering his strongest form and having learned a lot, gave Ugochukwu a solid platform for the winter and set him up well for the season ahead.

READ MORE

What To Watch For: A few key talking points ahead of the title decider in Madrid

How To Watch Round 9 in Madrid: TV, Session Times and More

The 19-year-old was impressive in post-season testing with his new team Campos. He then started the year off by beating Slater to the Formula Regional Oceania Trophy in New Zealand.

Ugochukwu carried that form into the opening round in Melbourne where he would go on to win the Feature Race.

MULTIPLE PODIUMS

Ugochukwu has been achieved six podiums this season, with five of those being in the Feature Races.

So far only Slater’s eight podiums are more than his, with his TRIDENT rival also having six on Sundays.

Ugochukwu has scored heavily in the Feature Races to build his title challenge

Scoring heavily in the Feature Races is where these two have separated themselves from the rest as this is where the big points are scored.

But the Sprints are also important, and in the first half of the season he scored points in three out of the five Saturday races – including a victory at Silverstone where he won by a record 17-second margin.

DOMINANT RACE PACE AND DARING WHEEL-TO-WHEEL ACTIONS

That form on Saturdays and Sundays has been built on some outstanding race pace, as shown by Ugochukwu’s ability to win a race by over 17s in Formula 3.

But that same weekend in the Feature Race, he went from 12th on the grid to third, carving his way through the field.

In Budapest, the Campos driver went from sixth to second on Sunday and was right on the back of Slater. But he just did not have enough overspeed to get past his rival into Turns 1 and 2.

This race showed the pace he has but also how brave he is in wheel-to-wheel racing, as Ugochukwu double move around the outside of Brando Badoer and Mattia Colnaghi will live long in the memory.

Ugochukwu has shown incredible race pace this season

But arguably this past weekend in Monza was Ugochukwu’s best display of both. After starting near the rear of the field in both races, he made his way up to P13 in the Sprint.

In the Feature, he was spun around in the early stages, and dropped to the back of the field, but yet still showed great pace and bravery to come through the field and finish in P8.

In a race where Slater failed to finish, those four points might prove critical in the title fight.

READ MORE

Taito Kato’s Monza Weekend Debrief

Ugochukwu on ‘full attack’ in Madrid title fight after impressive fightback in Monza

WHAT MUST IMPROVE IN MADRID

Ugochukwu and Campos need to regain their form in Qualifying especially at Madrid – a circuit where many drivers feel could be tough to overtake around.

The American qualified in the top five in each of the opening four rounds, but since then his Friday form has taken a slight dip.

The Campos driver and his team will want to have a clean weekend in Madrid

Ugochukwu was at the back of the top 10 at Silverstone and Spa-Francorchamps and sixth in Budapest. In Monza he was 10th in Group A and started in P23.

On top of that, the 19-year-old has picked up a few penalties recently at Spa, Budapest and Monza that have put him on the back foot.

The positive is at the in-season test in Madrid last month, Ugochukwu set the fastest time overall and was the quickest driver in two out of the four sessions.

So Ugochukwu and Campos know they can be quick at the Madring circuit, and if they have a clean Friday, they most definitely have the pace to come out on top.

Next Up

title: Rodin Motorsport confirms Niccolò Maccagnani for the final round in Madrid
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport has confirmed that Niccolò Maccagnani will be racing for the team in Madrid.

Maccagnani, a member of the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy, is set to take the step up to Formula 3 having spent a season in Italian F4 where he has two wins and four podiums in total.

Prior to that, the 16-year-old finished second in the 2025 Formula Trophy and fourth overall in the Formula 4 South East Asia Championship.

Maccagnani now steps up to F3 with Rodin, replacing Christian Ho for the final round of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 season.

title: What To Watch For: A few key talking points ahead of the title decider in Madrid
excerpt:
A special few months of racing is set to come to an end as we approach the final round of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 season in Madrid.

The newest venue on the calendar hosts the finale, with both championships still yet to be decided. On top of that, there are several drivers and teams aiming to sign of in style.

So before we head out of the pitlane as the Madring here is everything we think you should be keeping an eye on this weekend…

THE TITLE CHASING TWO

Just 15 points separate Freddie Slater and Ugo Ugochukwu at the top of the Championship Standings, and Madrid will see the climax of an all-time great title fight.

Slater has had the upper hand in recent rounds. Since Silverstone, the TRIDENT driver has scored 55 points, while his rival has achieved just 22 in that period.

In addition to that, the Briton has had two pole positions at Spa-Francorchamps and Monza, while was second in Budapest.

Slater and Ugochukwu are set to battle it out for the title in Madrid

As for Ugochukwu, he was only in the top 12 at Budapest and has been forced to fight through the field in Belgium and most recently at the Temple of Speed.

But the Campos Racing driver will take pride from the fact that he has fought through more often that not, and also that he still has a massive chance to win.

READ MORE

How To Watch Round 9 in Madrid: TV, Session Times and More

Taito Kato’s Monza Weekend Debrief

Ugochukwu will also take confidence from the fact that he set the fastest time of the Madrid test, although Slater also excelled – with both drivers leading two sessions apiece.

So both will believe that it could be them standing with the biggest prize come the end of the weekend, and they have shown a willingness to also go wheel-to-wheel with each other.

It sets up a fascinating final round, and for our first race weekend in Madrid, what more could we ask for?

Rivera and Nael are distant contenders for the title as well this weekend

THE BATTLE FOR THIRD (AND MAYBE THE TITLE)

Ugochukwu and Slater are not the only drivers with something to fight for, every other member of the grid will have their own agendas.

For example, both Ugochukwu’s teammates Ernesto Rivera and Théophile Nael are mathematically still in with a chance of winning the title.

Now it is a longshot and it will take a lot for that to happen, but outside of that, both drivers will want to make sure that they are on the championship podium.

However they are not alone in those desires, as just 32 points separate Rivera in third to Mattia Colnaghi in 13th.

If you extend that even more, the gap from Rivera to Alessandro Giusti in 20th is 53 points, and while it is a tall order for the MP Motorsport driver, it shows how tight things are in the midfield.

So each of these drivers will know that a strong weekend in Madrid could transform their position in the final Standings.

With three races on offer it is a chance for several drivers to climb up the Standings

It will also give them a lot of momentum going into the winter and into their next season of racing.

TRIDENT AIMING TO STOP CAMPOS

The drivers will have their own agendas but so will the teams, especially Campos and TRIDENT.

Going into the weekend, the gap between the top two is 64 points, which means they are on the brink of winning their second consecutive Teams’ Title.

READ MORE

Ugochukwu on ‘full attack’ in Madrid title fight after impressive fightback in Monza

Lacorte revels in ‘special’ Feature Race victory at home in Monza

But the Spanish outfit might have feared that lead being cut down on Friday afternoon in Monza, when Freddie Slater and Matteo De Palo qualified on the front row – while Ugochukwu and Nael were down the order.

However De Palo’s technical infringement, and Slater’s mechanical issue that caused him to retire from the Feature mean TRIDENT’s hopes of cutting majorly into Campos’ advantage were dented.

They still have a chance, however, and head to Madrid with momentum. But Campos know that if they perform at the level they have shown all season, they will have the title wrapped up.

The drivers will face the challenge of racing around Madrid for first time

A NEW VENUE AND NEW FORMAT

An added factor coming into this weekend is one that we cannot forget – and that is Madrid is a new venue.

While the drivers and teams got their first taste of the track in last month’s test, race weekends are very different, especially this one.

There will be two Qualifying sessions and two Feature Races this weekend. This means the drivers and teams have two races on Saturday – the Sprint and Feature Race 1.

This puts a lot of pressure on the drivers but also their teams, but it is also means there is more opportunity for success.

It will be a brand-new weekend for everyone, adding another layer of intrigue to what is already an exciting first visit to Madrid.
